messages:
service-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming route `/v1/stream` p99 latency breach detected (p99=3.8s, SLO=1.5s) across region-us-west-2. Auto-escalation -> page oncall.
jo_oncall: Saw the bot. I’m on it. First glance: spike coincides with increased streaming stalls and partial chunk timeouts reported by clients (acme-payments). Marking impact: high for streaming sessions (>5min sessions dropped).
jo_oncall: Checking recent infra telemetry: GPU pool `gpu-pool-2` shows tail latency jump and a single node with rising ECC correctable counts. Pulling NVML now.
ash_l3: pinged — I can help with nvml logs and kernel dmesg. If ECC or thermal, we'll need to triage node-level and either evacuate or fence.
maya_sre: @jo_oncall @ash_l3 If it's thermal/ECC flake, fast mitigation is to drain the node and shift traffic to fallback nodes and ramp a warm spare. Also consider model downgrade for long streams to lower memory usage.
jo_oncall: Commanded `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,temperature.gpu,fan.speed,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 2` — seeing GPU0 temp 87C, fan 32%, util 94% util, memory high on that pod.
ash_l3: grabbing ECC counters now.
ash_l3: ````
# nvml -- summarized
GPU: gpu0
ECC (correctable) 10m delta: 118 -> 298
Thermal Throttle events: 7 in last 15m
Power Limit Clamped: false
Temperature: 85-87C
````
ash_l3: dmesg shows intermittent `GPU: Correctable ECC error` messages and `GPU thermal trip` warnings. Looks like a flaky card starting to produce correctable errors and thermal throttles. Probably hardware-level.
jeva_support: customer reports: "we started seeing stalls at ~18:02 UTC, multiple aborted streams, reconnect loops" — they can route traffic to another region but want status.
jo_oncall: Mitigation plan (live): 1) Evacuate pods off gpu-node-42, 2) Drain node, 3) Route new streaming sessions to `gpu-pool-1` and warm an extra node, 4) Apply model fallback for existing long-lived sessions.
jo_oncall: Executing drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — starting now, moving scheduled pods.
maya_sre: I'll trigger autoscaler to add one warm GPU node to `gpu-pool-1` and increase `streaming-burst` capacity temporarily. Also enabling `route_override` for streaming route to `model-redwood-lite` for slow sessions.
ash_l3: For graceful migration we should trim max chunk size to 256 tokens and reduce `keepalive` to drop very slow consumers.
jo_oncall: Applied runtime override: `POST /admin/routes/override { route: "/v1/stream", model: "redwood-lite", max_chunk_tokens: 256 }` — responses should be shorter but keep clients alive. :thumbsup:
service-bot: Deploy bot: `evacuate-node` job completed for gpu-node-42, 12 pods rescheduled.
ash_l3: After drain: ECC correctable rate dropped on the cluster but GPU0 still shows rising ECC counts in host logs — node should be quarantined for hardware replacement.
jo_oncall: Customer impact summary so far: acme-payments experienced ~150 aborted streaming sessions in the window 18:02-18:28 UTC. We routed ~90% of new sessions to fallback successfully. Post-mitigation p99 for /v1/stream dropped to 1.6s (close to SLO), p95 back to 0.9s.
maya_sre: Good. Recommend marking node `quarantine=true` and remove from the scheduler pool until hardware swap. Create ticket for HW replacement.
ash_l3: Collected logs and attached to INC ticket: INC-2026-1342. Saved `nvml` dump and `dmesg` fragments.
jo_oncall: Handoff to @maya_sre for follow-up and RCA. Summary: thermal + ECC correctables on gpu-node-42 caused tail latency and streaming stalls. Live mitigation performed: drain + routing override + warm spare. Customer notified via support.
maya_sre: Taking it. I'll coordinate with infra procurement and open a hardware incident with vendor. Also schedule a postmortem: collect kernel logs, NVML, fan controller firmware, and AV tests.
eva_support: I've updated acme-payments with a mitigation note and ETA for follow-up. They requested an interim SLA credit evaluation.
jo_oncall: Closing on-call rotation note: alert resolved for now, monitoring for 60m. If p99 creeps back up we escalate to L4 vendor. :white_check_mark:
maya_sre: Action items: ["Quarantine gpu-node-42", "Open HW RMA with vendor (INC-2026-1342)", "Run extended memtest on replacement node", "Tune autoscaler runbooks for warmer pool"]. Assigning owners in the ticket.
service-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-1342 created and linked to thread.
jo_oncall: Thanks team. Good rapid mitigation. Will add logs to the incident thread and draft a short customer-facing blameless note.
